message.content:
**Logistic regression** is a statistical method used to model the relationship between one or more predictor variables and a binary (two‑class) outcome. Instead of predicting a continuous value, it predicts the probability that the outcome belongs to a particular class. ### Key features | Feature | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Outcome variable** | Binary (e.g., 0/1, yes/no, success/failure). | | **Model form** | Uses the logistic (sigmoid) function to map a linear combination of predictors to a probability between 0 and 1:
\(\displaystyle P(Y=1|X)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-(\beta_0+\beta_1X_1+\dots+\beta_kX_k)}}\) | | **Link function** | Logit link: \(\text{logit}(P)=\ln\!\big(\frac{P}{1-P}\big)=\beta_0+\beta_1X_1+\dots+\beta_kX_k\). | | **Estimation** | Parameters \(\beta\) are estimated by maximum likelihood (MLE). | | **Interpretation** | Coefficients represent the change in the log‑odds of the outcome per unit change in the predictor. Exponentiating gives odds ratios. | | **Extensions** | • Multinomial logistic regression (more than two unordered categories)
• Ordinal logistic regression (ordered categories)
• Penalized logistic regression (L1/L2 regularization) | ### Why use logistic regression? - **Probabilistic output**: Provides a probability estimate, useful for risk scoring. - **Interpretability**: Coefficients can be interpreted in terms of odds ratios. - **Efficiency**: Works well with small to moderate sample sizes and a moderate number of predictors. - **Baseline model**: Often used as a baseline for comparison with more complex classifiers. ### Example Suppose we want to predict whether a patient has a disease (1) or not (0) based on age and blood pressure: \[ \text{logit}(P) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \times \text{Age} + \beta_2 \times \text{BP} \] After fitting the model, we might find: - \(\beta_0 = -5.0\) - \(\beta_1 = 0.04\) (each additional year increases log‑odds by 0.04) - \(\beta_2 = 0.02\) (each mmHg increase in BP increases log‑odds by 0.02) For a 60‑year‑old patient with BP 140: \[ \text{logit}(P) = -5.0 + 0.04(60) + 0.02(140) = 1.8 \] \[ P = \frac{1}{1+e^{-1.8}} \approx 0.86 \] So the model estimates an 86 % probability of disease. --- **In short:** Logistic regression is a simple yet powerful tool for binary classification that models the probability of an event using a logistic function applied to a linear combination of predictors.
